newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan economic recovery still gradual - BOJ governor.
newsitem.headline: Japan economic recovery still gradual - BOJ governor.

text.p: Japan's economy is continuing to recover gradually but factors such as competition from Asian economies and balance-sheet adjustments are hindering the pace of that recovery, Bank of Japan (BOJ) governor Yasuo Matsushita said in a speech on Wednesday.
Matsushita said the central bank's monetary policy was geared towards ensuring economic recovery.
He said the mechanisms for economic growth led by private demand could now be seen, "but it is necessary to make sure that the economic recovery is a sustainable one".
Matsushita said the economy had returned to a recovery track following the correction of the surge in the yen's value and various economic steps taken by the government.
"The economy is continuing to recover gradually," he said.
"The economy is continuing to recover gradually," he said.
Matsushita said the reason the word "gradual" had not yet been dropped was because factors encouraging recovery and pressure from structural adjustments were affecting the economy at the same time.

The factors working to encourage recovery were government policies such as low interest rates, which he said have helped a rebound in housing investment and corporate capital investment. Fiscal stimulative measures have also helped support overall demand, he said.
Optimistic sentiment among companies towards corporate investment and employment was starting to spread with an increase in corporate profits, Matsushita said.
Last year's worries about the possibility of a deflationary spiral have just about evaporated, he said.
"A cyclical economic recovery centring on private demand is slowly but steadily getting off the ground," he said.
On the other hand, factors restraining growth were pressure from inventory adjustments and competition from economies in other parts of Asia, Matsushita said.
He said corporate capital investment, although recovering gradually, had not yet recovered completely due to stock adjustments and repayment of debt.
Matsushita said a flow of cheap imports from Asia had contributed to an decrease in capital investment within Japan.
The moving of production facilities overseas by large Japanese companies has also capped enthusiasm for increasing corporate investment due to lower orders from the firms, he said.
He said some business managers remained uncertain about their business outlook and about ways to revitalise their firms' fortunes.
